stem.en: Fish lay 100s to 1000s of eggs at a time, with low survival of young ones. Frogs lay 5,000 to 50,000, low. Lizards lay 2 to 20, moderate. Birds lay 1 to 15, moderate to high. Which statement fits these figures?

text.en: More eggs at a time goes with higher survival

feedback.en: It is the other way round. The most eggs go with low survival.

text.en: Animals with few eggs lose all of their young ones

feedback.en: Lizards and birds have moderate or higher survival, so they do not lose all.

text.en: Egg number and survival are equal in all four

feedback.en: Both egg number and survival differ between these animals.

text.en: Fewer eggs go with a better chance for each

feedback.en: Yes. As the number of eggs falls, each young one has a better chance.

explanation.en: The animals with the most eggs have low survival, and those with the fewest have moderate to high survival. Each young one of a bird has a better chance than each young one of a frog.

hints.en: Read the egg numbers and the survival words together.
Which animal has both the fewest eggs and the best survival?
